Appearance:
 Shri Harshad Bahrani - Advocate for appellant.
 Shri C.P. Singh - Government Advocate for the State.

Order 
1. Record of both the Courts below are available.

2. This appeal under Section 71(6) of Food Safety and Standards Act has been filed against the judgment dated 03.09.2025 passed in RCA No.72/2025 by Principal District Judge and Appellate Authority under Food Safety and Standards Act, Gwalior, thereby dismissing the appeal filed against the order dated 27.12.2024 passed by the Additional District Magistrate & Adjudicating Officer,
District Gwalior, in Case No. Q/Food Safety/17/2024, wherein, for breach of Section 26(2)(ii),
punishable under Section 51 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, a penalty of Rs. 2 lacs has been imposed on appellant.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Act, Gwalior
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. It is submitted by counsel for appellant that, as per the report of the Food Analyst, the sample of milk was found to be sub-standard and it was found to be a mixture of cow and buffalo milk.
It is submitted that no hazardous component was found in the sample; therefore, the penalty of Rs. 2 Lacs is on the higher side.

4 . Per contra , it is submitted by counsel for the State that, generally cow NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:1741 2 MSA-94-2025 milk is more suitable for infant babies, and if appellant was Satpal Singh Kukreja vs M P State Through The Food Safety Officer ... on 14 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25712677/
1 selling milk which was a mixture of cow and buffalo milk, then the applicant was playing with the lives of infant babies, and therefore, it cannot be said that the sale of milk containing a mixture of cow and buffalo milk is not a heinous one.
5.

entities.text: Satpal Singh Kukreja vs M P State
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considered the submissions made by counsel for the parties.
6. Counsel for the appellant was directed to point out as to whether cow milk is given to infant babies or buffalo milk is given.

7. It is submitted by Shri Bahirani that, since cow milk is easily digested, therefore, it is preferred,
and generally, it is given to infant babies up to a certain age.

8. Thus, it is clear that milk which is a mixture of cow and buffalo milk may prove fatal or hazardous to the health of an infant baby, and since the appellant was involved in selling sub-standard milk,
therefore

, it cannot be said that the conduct of the appellant requires interference with the amount of penalty of Rs. 2 Lacs.
9.
No other arguments is advanced by counsel for the appellant.
10. As no case is made out warranting interference, accordingly, the MSA fails and is hereby dismissed.
(G. S. AHLUWALIA) JUDGE Aman Satpal Singh Kukreja vs M P State Through The Food Safety Officer ... on 14 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/25712677/
